newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 3.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.

- A prominent figure in the opposition Finna Fail party is believed to have received more than one million Irish pounds from Dunnes Stores in the early 1990s. A government resigned at the weekend because of payments from the company.

- Telecom firm ESAT Digiphone is threatening to pull out of its proposed deal with the police unless the agreement allowing its mobile telephone network to use police station masts is concluded by Friday.
- Press freedom provisions in the European Convention on Human Rights should be incorporated into the Irish Constitution, according to the newspaper industry.
- Ireland expects to export 830 million Irish pounds worth of beef to overseas markets by the end of the year despite the BSE crisis.
- The Irish President, Mary Robinson warned on Monday that politicians must be careful with their language if a lasting peace in Northern Ireland is to be achieved.
- The government has signalled a further rise in unemployment after 1998.
- The government is preparing to offer a tax sweetener worth close to one billion Irish pounds to help secure agreement on a new national pay deal.
- The Irish National Teachers' Organisation has named 47 "seriously sub-standard" primary schools and warned that it would take action to secure urgently needed improvements.
- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, commenting on the resignation of government minister Michael Lowry, said on Monday there was one law for everybody and everybody must comply with it.
- Small Irish businesses stand to lose out on 20 million Irish pounds in soft loans unless AIB manages to fully lend its share of the Access to Finance Scheme before the end of the year.
